title_en: Guiding Case No. 261: Zhang et al. — criminal附带 civil public interest litigation for illegal mining
ruling_gist_en:
1. For crimes against environmental resource protection that cross administrative divisions, where the circumstances meet the provisions of Article 20, Paragraph 2 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, a higher people's court may designate a lower people's court with environmental resource trial functions to have jurisdiction.

2. Where it is more appropriate to organize ecological environment restoration at the damaged site, the people's court may transfer the restoration funds that have been executed to the relevant departments of the damaged site across administrative divisions for ecological environment restoration.

full_text_en:
Guiding Case No. 261: Zhang A et al. — criminal附带 civil public interest litigation for illegal mining

(Adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court and released on May 26, 2025)

Keywords

criminal / criminal附带 civil public interest litigation / crime of illegal mining / cross-administrative division / designated jurisdiction / restoration of damaged site

Ruling Gist

1. For cross-administrative division cases of crimes against environmental resources protection, where the circumstances specified in Article 20, Paragraph 2 of the *Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China* are met, a superior people's court may designate a subordinate people's court with environmental resources adjudication functions to have jurisdiction.

2. Where it is more appropriate to organize and implement ecological environment restoration at the damaged site, the people's court may transfer the restoration funds that have been executed across administrative divisions to the relevant departments at the damaged site for ecological environment restoration.

Basic Facts

From March to July 2021, defendants Zhang A, Zhang B, Li, Ding, et al. provided capital, defendants Hong, Wang, et al. provided "three-no" sand dredging vessels (vessels without vessel certificates, registration, or inspection), and together with the pre-arranged sand purchasing vessel owners defendants Zhang C, Ling, Bao, et al., without obtaining a river channel sand mining license, in the upper and lower sections of the river reach of the Freshwater Dolphin National Nature Reserve in the Tongling section of the Yangtze River in Anhui Province, through an integrated dredging and transportation method, jointly illegally dredged and transported 46,765.04 tons of river sand, valued at RMB 2,893,129 (currency unit same below). Defendant Ma, knowing that the river sand was illegally mined, still purchased 1,700 tons and sold them. Upon appraisal, the illegal sand mining by Zhang A and others caused ecological environment damage to the Yangtze River, and there is a causal relationship between the act and the ecological environment damage at the incident site. The assessed amount of ecological environment damage to the Yangtze River was RMB 5,157,476.86, including RMB 4,910,329.2 for riverbed structure damage, RMB 96,146.02 for fish resource damage, RMB 14,884.62 for benthos damage, RMB 101,557.02 for biodiversity service value damage, and RMB 34,560 for follow-up monitoring costs.

It was also found that the period from June 1 to September 30 each year is the prohibited mining period for sand mining in the main river channel of the Yangtze River below Yibin. The upper and lower sections of the river reach of the Freshwater Dolphin National Nature Reserve in the Tongling section of the Yangtze River in Anhui Province are prohibited mining areas for river sand. From January 2020 until the incident, no sand mining licenses had been issued for the Anhui section of the Yangtze River.

The Jianhu County People's Procuratorate of Jiangsu Province charged defendants Zhang A and others with the crime of illegal mining, and defendant Ma with the crime of concealing and disguising criminal proceeds, and initiated a public prosecution to the people's court. At the same time, on the grounds that public social interests were harmed, it initiated a collateral civil public interest lawsuit, requesting that Zhang A and others be ordered to bear joint and several liability for compensation for ecological environment damage, and to make a public apology to the public in national media, etc. Because the case had a long duration of criminal acts and the crime scene spanned provincial administrative divisions such as Anhui and Jiangsu, the Supreme People's Court designated the Dongtai City People's Court of Jiangsu Province to hear this case. This court is one of the grassroots courts with cross-regional jurisdiction for environmental resources adjudication designated by the Jiangsu High People's Court based on the needs of ecological environment protection within the province.

Judgment

The Dongtai City People's Court of Jiangsu Province, on March 1, 2022, rendered criminal附带 civil public interest judgment No. (2022) Su 0981 Xingchu 46, finding defendants Zhang A and others guilty of the crime of illegal mining, sentencing them to fixed-term imprisonment ranging from four years and six months to one year respectively, applying probation to some defendants, imposing fines ranging from RMB 200,000 to RMB 15,000 respectively, and recovering illegal gains; defendant Ma was found guilty of the crime of concealing and disguising criminal proceeds, sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of one year and six months, with a two-year probation, and a fine of RMB 20,000, and recovery of illegal gains; the defendants in the collateral civil public interest action, Zhang A and others, were ordered to jointly and severally compensate for ecological environment damage of RMB 5,157,476.86 within the scope of the amount of sand each participated in mining, and to make a public apology in national media, etc. After the judgment was pronounced, there was no appeal or protest, and the judgment has become legally effective.

After the judgment took effect, the Dongtai City People's Court of Jiangsu Province transferred the executed ecological environment restoration funds to the Tongling Intermediate People's Court of Anhui Province, and jointly with the local government implemented the Tongling Yangtze River ecological environment remediation and finless porpoise protection project.

Reasoning

The Yangtze River is the mother river of the Chinese nation and an important support for its development. Sand and gravel in the Yangtze River channel are national mineral resources. Illegal mining of river sand will damage the ecological environment of the Yangtze River and affect the stability of the river regime, flood control, and navigation safety. Defendants Zhang A and others violated the provisions of the Mineral Resources Law, and without obtaining a river channel sand mining license, illegally engaged in sand mining during the prohibited mining period and in prohibited mining areas of the Yangtze River, reaching the circumstance of serious nature, and their acts constituted the crime of illegal mining. Defendant Ma, knowing that the purchased river sand was proceeds of crime from others, still purchased it, and his act constituted the crime of concealing and disguising criminal proceeds. The sand mining site involved in the case is located between the upper and lower sections of the river reach of the Freshwater Dolphin National Nature Reserve in the Tongling section of Anhui Province, an area that is a habitat for precious and endangered aquatic wild animals such as the Chinese sturgeon and the finless porpoise. The illegal sand mining by Zhang A and others directly caused damage to the ecosystem of the Yangtze River waters where the incident occurred, destroyed the breeding and living environment of aquatic animal resources, and upon appraisal, caused ecological environment damage to the Yangtze River of RMB 5,157,476.86. Pursuant to Article 93 of the *Yangtze River Protection Law of the People's Republic of China* and Articles 1168 and 1235 of the *Civil Code of the People's Republic of China*, Zhang A and others shall bear joint and several civil liability for compensating the ecological environment damage of the Yangtze River within the scope of the amount of illegal sand each participated in. There are two focal issues in this case: first, the issue of jurisdiction over the case; second, the issue of the use of ecological environment restoration funds.

Regarding the issue of jurisdiction over the case. Article 20, Paragraph 2 of the *Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China* (Fa Shi [2021] No. 1) provides: "Where it is more appropriate for a case to be tried by a people's court other than the place of the crime or the domicile of the defendant, the superior people's court may designate a subordinate people's court to have jurisdiction." In this case, the defendants who committed illegal sand mining were numerous and the criminal acts lasted for a long time, and the sand mining locations and sand selling locations spanned multiple administrative divisions such as Anhui and Jiangsu. The illegal sand mining involved in the case had characteristics such as huge profits, gang operations, and collusion between internal and external parties, and there were clues of suspected crimes by local public officials. Therefore, it was more appropriate to designate a people's court outside Anhui Province to hear the case. Considering factors such as the level of correspondence, convenience, and professionalism of the investigation, prosecution, and adjudication activities, the Supreme People's Court designated the Dongtai City People's Court of Jiangsu Province, which has environmental resources adjudication functions, to have jurisdiction over this case.

Regarding the issue of the use of ecological environment restoration funds. The protection of the ecological environment of the Yangtze River basin should adhere to the principle of systematic governance and priority of on-site restoration. Ecological environment restoration funds are the basic guarantee for the implementation of restoration. In most cases, because the ecological environment damage occurs within the jurisdictional area of the trial court, the restoration funds can be matched with the restoration implementation. However, in cross-domain situations, especially cross-provincial administrative divisions, it is difficult to use ecological restoration funds for the implementation of ecological environment restoration at the damaged site. Although this case was designated by the Supreme People's Court to be tried by the Dongtai City People's Court of Jiangsu Province, the damaged site is located in the Tongling section of the Yangtze River in Anhui Province. The illegal sand mining by Zhang A and others caused serious damage to the local Yangtze River ecological environment. If timely and effective restoration is not carried out, it will inevitably lead to the persistence or even aggravation of the damage consequences. After the judgment in this case took effect, the people's court promptly transferred the executed ecological environment restoration funds to the relevant departments of Tongling City, Anhui Province, for use in the ecological environment restoration work of the damaged site in the Tongling section of the Yangtze River in Anhui Province.

Relevant Laws

Article 1168, Article 1234, Article 1235 of the *Civil Code of the People's Republic of China*

Article 28, Article 93 of the *Yangtze River Protection Law of the People's Republic of China*

Article 27 of the *Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China*

Article 20 of the *Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China* (Fa Shi [2021] No. 1)
